acceptance_criteria: New public module `swx_io::glb` with `pub fn write_glb(positions: &[[f32; 3]], indices: &[u32], out: &mut impl Write) -> Result<(), GlbError>`, re-exported from the crate root, with a doc comment citing the glTF 2.0 specification.

Output layout: 12-byte header (magic `0x46546C67`, version `2`, total length equal to the number of bytes written, all little-endian `u32`); a JSON chunk (type `0x4E4F534A`) padded with spaces (`0x20`) to a multiple of 4 bytes; then a BIN chunk (type `0x004E4942`) padded with zeros to a multiple of 4 bytes.

The JSON has `asset.version` `"2.0"`, one scene with one node, one mesh with one primitive in mode `4` (triangles), a `POSITION` accessor (componentType `5126`, type `VEC3`, with `min` and `max` equal to the exact per-axis bounds of `positions`) and an index accessor (componentType `5125`, type `SCALAR`), one buffer, and two bufferViews (positions first at byteOffset 0, target `34962`; indices next, target `34963`). Positions are stored unchanged in millimetres, and the node has `scale` `[0.001, 0.001, 0.001]`, because glTF units are metres.

A documented `GlbError` with variants for: index count not a multiple of 3, index out of range, a non-finite coordinate, an empty mesh (no triangles), and an I/O error. Every check runs before the first byte is written, so on error `out` receives nothing. Nothing panics on bad input. (Reusing the STL validation is fine.)
Writing the same mesh twice gives byte-identical output.

Tests (reading the bytes back inside the test, no new dev-dependencies): for a 10 × 20 × 30 mm box (8 vertices, 12 triangles), the header length equals the output length; both chunk lengths are multiples of 4; the JSON parses with `serde_json`, the accessor counts are 8 and 36, and `min`/`max` are `[0, 0, 0]` and `[10, 20, 30]`; the BIN chunk is 240 bytes (96 position bytes and 144 index bytes) and its floats and indices equal the input exactly; and each of the five error cases gives its variant, with an empty `Vec<u8>` afterwards.
All existing `swx-io` tests pass unchanged; no test is weakened or removed. No `unsafe`.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
objective.description: M4-04b: swx-io: binary glTF 2.0 (GLB) writer for an indexed triangle mesh
